official.deadline_note: Posse publishes no single deadline: nomination timelines and deadlines vary by Posse city or program, nominations are accepted in the spring and summer before senior year begins, and Posse directs applicants to contact their local Posse office for specific deadlines at the start of every calendar year.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle: nominations in spring and summer before senior year begins; Dynamic Assessment Process September to December; Scholars celebrated at winter Awards Ceremonies
official.status_note: Posse's nomination pages are live and describe an annual, repeating recruitment cycle with no closed round announced; exact nomination windows vary by city and program and are confirmed by the local Posse office.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Each Posse Scholar wins a full-tuition scholarship to attend one of Posse's partner colleges or universities, and partner institutions provide Posse Scholars with full-tuition scholarships, weekly faculty mentoring, and other support.
benefits: Full-tuition scholarship to attend one of Posse's partner colleges or universities

Pre-Collegiate Training: weekly two-hour workshops with staff trainers and Posse peers from January to August of senior year, covering team building, cross-cultural communication, leadership and academic excellence

Campus Program: Posse staff visit each university four times a year, and each mentor meets weekly with the Posse as a team and with each Scholar individually every two weeks during the first two years
Annual weekend-long PossePlus Retreat attended by the wider student body, faculty and administration
Career Program with 250-plus career partners and the Fellowship Program, through which Scholars and alumni have won more than 600 national fellowships since 2001
Posse Access: unselected finalists can opt to have their profiles shared with partner institutions for regular admission
eligibility: Be nominated by their high school or a community-based organization in one of Posse's recruitment cities
Be in the first term of their senior year in high school
Demonstrate leadership within their high school, community or family
Apply on time; nominations are accepted in the spring and summer before senior year begins, with timelines varying by Posse city or program
The Posse Scholarship is neither a minority nor a need-based scholarship and is open to students of all backgrounds
requirements: Nomination by a high school or community-based organization registered with Posse, since Posse does not accept direct applications
Completion and submission of the Posse application through the Nominee Portal
Participation in Posse's Dynamic Assessment Process, a three-part assessment of large-group and individual interviews running September to December
RSVP for Posse interview dates through the Nominee Portal

City-specific rules may apply; for example Posse D.C. requires students to reside or attend school in D.C., Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Arlington County, Fairfax County or Alexandria City, and to be open to an early decision commitment if selected as a finalist
documents: Nomination submitted by the high school or community-based organization through the Posse nominator portal
Posse application completed and submitted through the Nominee Portal
RSVP for Posse interview dates through the Nominee Portal
selection_criteria: Leaders in their high schools and communities
Committed to their education and demonstrating academic potential
Positive, motivated, talented, ambitious young people

Performance across the Dynamic Assessment Process, which uses nontraditional forums and large-group and individual interviews; Posse staff and partner college administrators select a diverse group of 10 students for each institution
coverage: Full tuition at a Posse partner college or university, awarded as a four-year, full-tuition leadership scholarship
application_method: A registered high school or community-based organization in a Posse recruitment city nominates the student, as early as the second semester of junior year
The nominee signs in to the Nominee Portal to update, complete and submit the Posse application and to RSVP for interview dates
The nominee takes part in the Dynamic Assessment Process from September to December, including large-group and individual interviews
Finalists commit to a partner institution through an early decision process if selected
Contact the local Posse office at the start of every calendar year for that city's nomination timeline and deadlines
official.application_route: Nomination only: a registered high school or community-based organization in a Posse city nominates the student, who then completes the Posse application in the Nominee Portal and attends the Dynamic Assessment Process.
official.study_mode: Full-time undergraduate study at a Posse partner college
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship rule is published; students must be nominated in one of Posse's U.S. recruitment cities or Puerto Rico, and individual city pages add local rules such as Posse D.C.'s requirement to reside or attend school in D.C., Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Arlington County, Fairfax County or Alexandria City.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction for the general Posse Scholarship. Posse's STEM Program separately seeks seniors with demonstrated STEM interest who have taken four years of math and four years of science and the most challenging courses offered, and the Posse Arts Program requires an audition or portfolio as candidates advance; the Posse Veterans Program recruits post-9/11 U.S. veterans nationwide.
official.duration: Four years of undergraduate study at a Posse partner college or university
official.description: Posse Scholars receive full-tuition leadership scholarships from Posse's partner colleges and universities after being nominated by their high school or a community-based organization in one of Posse's recruitment cities. Posse describes the scholarship as neither a minority nor a need-based award, open to students of all backgrounds, and supports each cohort of 10 students with pre-college training, on-campus mentoring and alumni programming.
official.region: United States (20-plus recruitment cities and Puerto Rico)

not_confirmed: funding_amount: Posse publishes no per-scholar dollar figure on any official page, only cumulative totals such as $2.65 billion awarded since 1989 and city totals like $543 million for New York
english_requirement: no English test or medium-of-instruction rule is published
deadline_central: no central deadline exists; nomination windows vary by Posse city or program
international_eligibility: the official pages do not address international students
required documents: no document checklist is published beyond the nomination, the Nominee Portal application and interview RSVPs
verification.notes: Award wording, eligibility, nomination-only route, DAP timing (September to December), support programmes and the D.C.-specific city rules were verified against Posse's own pages; the per-scholar amount remains unconfirmed because partner-college tuition varies and Posse publishes only cumulative dollar totals.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply directly for this scholarship: a high school or community-based organization registered with Posse in one of Posse's recruitment cities must nominate you, and nominators can put students forward as early as the second semester of junior year. Once nominated, you complete and submit the Posse application in the Nominee Portal and go through the Dynamic Assessment Process from September to December, a three-month mix of large-group and individual interviews from which a team of 10 students is chosen for each partner college. Winning means four years of full tuition at a selective partner college plus weekly workshops, on-campus mentoring and a built-in peer network, but Posse publishes no living stipend, so families should budget separately for room, board, books and personal costs. Because nomination windows differ by city, contact your local Posse office at the very start of the calendar year for that year's dates.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High school seniors in Posse's recruitment cities with a genuine leadership record in school, family or community who want full tuition at selective partner colleges and can commit to weekly workshops and ongoing mentoring.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your city recruits: Atlanta, Bay Area, Boston, Chicago, D.C., Houston, Los Angeles, Miami, New Orleans, New York, Puerto Rico, or a Virtual Program city (New Jersey, Philadelphia, Tennessee, Twin Cities, Virginia)
Ask your school or community organization whether it is registered to nominate; if not, have it contact the local Posse office to register as a nominator
Call or email your local Posse office in January to get that year's nomination window, since deadlines vary by city and program
As a nominee, complete the Portal application promptly and RSVP for every interview date offered in the September to December DAP window
Review the partner colleges that recruit from your city and decide which you would genuinely attend, since finalists must commit early
For Arts or STEM tracks, prepare an audition or portfolio, or evidence four years of math and science with the most challenging courses offered
common_rejection_risks: Missing the local nomination window, which opens in spring or summer before senior year and differs by city and program
Having no registered nominator: individual applications are not accepted, so outstanding students without a nominating school or organization never reach the process
Performing poorly in DAP group exercises, which are designed to surface collaborative leadership rather than individual dominance
A weak or inconsistent academic trajectory, since although there is no GPA minimum only nominees who have consistently progressed toward academic excellence advance
Ruling out the partner colleges recruiting from your city, or refusing an early decision commitment as a finalist
Misreading the award as need-based or minority-only and preparing an application around financial hardship rather than demonstrated leadership
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Room, board, books, personal expenses and travel to and from campus: Posse publishes tuition coverage only and states no stipend, housing or travel allowance.
document_audit: Posse publishes no document checklist, so keep your nomination confirmation from your nominator as evidence you are in the process
Complete every section of the Nominee Portal application rather than leaving it partial, since the portal is both the application and the interview scheduling system
Keep academic records and activity evidence ready for DAP, where academic trajectory is assessed without a formal transcript submission rule
Arts candidates should expect an audition or portfolio request as they advance through selection
alerts: Timing trap: nominations are accepted in the spring and summer before senior year and DAP runs September to December, so waiting until autumn of senior year can mean your city's window has already closed
The Posse Arts Program, Posse STEM Program and Posse Veterans Program run separate nomination processes with their own rules and cities
Some city pages impose local residency or school attendance rules, such as Posse D.C.'s requirement to reside or attend school in the D.C. metro counties
Finalists should expect an early decision style commitment to a single partner institution, which is binding
Unselected finalists are not automatically lost: they can opt into Posse Access to be visible to partner colleges for regular admission
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Nominator submits your nomination through the Posse nominator portal, you complete the application and RSVP for interviews in the Nominee Portal, attend the three-part Dynamic Assessment Process from September to December, then commit early to a partner college if selected as a finalist.
